en: I'm so excited to be here.

speaker: Unknown
en: Essentially, how to help them deal with hard stuff and do hard stuff and build hard things.
zh: 本质上，是如何帮助他们应对困难的事情，做困难的事情，并构建困难的事物。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I guess just broadly, does that ring a bell?
zh: 所以我想大概地问一下，这有印象吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Does that resonate?
zh: 这有共鸣吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, absolutely.
zh: 是的，绝对有。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's something I care a lot about.
zh: 这是我非常关心的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been, I think, pretty lucky in my career.
zh: 在我的职业生涯中，我想我非常幸运。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been very drawn to working on hard product problems, regulated areas, really hard business models, things with pretty high emotional stakes for the users of the products.
zh: 我一直非常致力于解决困难的产品问题、监管领域、真正困难的商业模式，以及那些对产品用户有很高情感风险的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're really likely to run into a lot of setbacks along the way.
zh: 在这个过程中，你真的很可能会遇到很多挫折。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think this is really relevant today because I look out and I talk to a lot of people and I hear fear and I hear uncertainty, and I think it comes from a few places.
zh: 我认为这在今天真的很有关系，因为我和很多人交谈，我听到恐惧，我听到不确定性，我认为这来自几个方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think obviously I'm really excited about AI and how it's transforming the way we work, and I think a lot of people are, but I think a lot of people are scared too.
zh: 我认为显然我对 AI 以及它如何改变我们的工作方式感到很兴奋，我想很多人也是，但我想很多人也很害怕。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're embracing these tools, they're learning these tools, but a lot of them have a question in the back of their mind, what does this mean for the future of my job?
zh: 他们正在拥抱这些工具，他们正在学习这些工具，但其中很多人心底都有一个疑问，这对我的工作未来意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And in many cases, what does this mean for my identity?
zh: 在很多情况下，这对我的身份意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it makes people question even just how we provide value as humans in society.
zh: 我想这甚至让人们质疑我们如何作为人类在社会中提供价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I also think people, especially young people, today haven't even necessarily been in a career environment where there wasn't always a thread of layoffs or things like that.
zh: 我还认为，人们，尤其是年轻人，今天甚至不一定处于一个没有裁员或类似情况线索的职业环境中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's taken a real psychic toll on a lot of people.
zh: 我认为这对很多人造成了真正的心理伤害。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think all managers now really need to be able to lead their teams through uncertainty, through fear, through hard things.
zh: 所以我认为现在所有的管理者真的都需要能够带领他们的团队通过不确定性，通过恐惧，通过困难的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I love the concept of taking a punch.
zh: 我喜欢“承受打击”这个概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've got a couple other tools that I like to use, but I think it can teach people how to thrive in these environments.
zh: 我有一些其他我喜欢使用的工具，但我认为它可以教人们如何在这些环境中茁壮成长。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's really important to me because I would love if more people took on hard things.
zh: 这对我来说真的很重要，因为我很乐意看到更多人承担困难的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's so many really hard challenging problems out there to solve.
zh: 我想外面有这么多真正困难的挑战性问题需要解决。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the more people are fearful about the future of their careers or the future of work, I think the more they gravitate toward things that they feel like they're likely to succeed at.
zh: 而且越是多的人对他们职业的未来或工作的未来感到恐惧，我认为他们越是倾向于那些他们觉得可能会成功的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's wonderful.
zh: 我认为这很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need that too, but I would really love it if more people were like, "Screw it.
zh: 我们也需要那个，但我真的很爱看到更多的人像是说，“管他呢。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to do something that's probably going to fail and it's important and it's worth doing and I'm going to do it well."
zh: 我要做一件可能会失败但很重要且值得做的事情，而且我要把它做好。”

speaker: Unknown
en: There's so many Venn diagrams of why this skill is so important, especially today.
zh: 有很多维恩图来解释为什么这项技能如此重要，尤其是今天。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is it feels like the easy stuff is done.
zh: 一个是感觉容易的事情已经做完了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The stuff left to build is hard.
zh: 剩下来要构建的东西是困难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like hardware, deep tech is where things are heading.
zh: 感觉硬件、深科技是事情发展的方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, just machine learning, AI skills, just stuff that's really hard.
zh: 还有，只是机器学习，AI 技能，只是那些真正困难的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the other is just AI is just changing so much.
zh: 然后另一点只是 AI 正在改变这么多。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just such a stressful time and hard time for a lot of people.
zh: 对很多人来说，这只是一个压力很大且艰难的时期。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's actually walk through some of the things that you have learned about how to help people get good at these things, about how to help people learn to take a punch, AKA do hard things, deal with struggle.
zh: 让我们实际走过一些你学到的东西，关于如何帮助人们擅长这些事情，关于如何帮助人们学会承受打击，也就是做困难的事情，应对挣扎。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first is you actually actively teach them.
zh: 第一点是你实际上主动教他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have specific tactics that you teach your team to deal with hardship and to take a punch.
zh: 你有具体的策略来教你的团队应对苦难和承受打击。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what are some of those things?
zh: 那么其中一些是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are some of the things that you teach your team and help them develop a skill?
zh: 你教你的团队一些什么来帮助他们发展一项技能？

speaker: Unknown
en: So at its core, when I say take a punch, what I mean is you're going to run into situations where something has gone wrong.
zh: 所以在其核心，当我说承受打击时，我的意思是你会遇到出问题的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe you have misstepped.
zh: 也许你走错了一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe you are just hearing someone speak critically about your work.
zh: 也许你只是听到某人批评你的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whatever it might be, you're going to feel like you have taken a punch.
zh: 无论可能是什么，你会觉得你承受了打击。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a very physical feeling.
zh: 这是一种非常生理的感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think as managers, you spend a lot of time teaching your team how to be successful.
zh: 我认为作为管理者，你会花很多时间教你的团队如何获得成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want to prepare them to maximize the chances of good outcome.
zh: 你想让他们做好准备，以最大化良好结果的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you don't also prepare them for what happens when that outcome isn't as good, you're going to run into some problems.
zh: 但如果你不让他们为当结果不尽如人意时会发生什么做好准备，你会遇到一些问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when I think about how to take a punch, what I say to my team is if they come to me and they're upset because something has happened, maybe they said something in a meeting that wasn't received well, or again, they're hearing somebody else talk about them in some way, whatever it is, I try to focus them less around whatever happened and how you litigate another person's impression of you based on something that has already happened, and more on what is the action that you can take next to counter program the narrative that you are afraid that this other person has of you.
zh: 所以当我思考如何承受打击时，我对我的团队说的是，如果他们来找我并且很心烦，因为发生了某些事，也许是他们在会议上说了些没被很好接受的话，或者又一次，他们听到别人以某种方式谈论他们，不管是什么，我试着让他们少关注发生的任何事情以及你如何根据已经发生的事情来争论另人对你的印象，而更多地关注你接下来能采取什么行动来反制你担心的这个人对你的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the counter program piece is really important.
zh: 我认为反制这部分真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because whenever we feel our egos injured, I think it's very natural for all of us to say like, "Well, that's not fair.
zh: 因为每当我们觉得自尊心受伤时，我认为我们所有人非常自然地会说，“嗯，那不公平。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to correct the record."
zh: 我想更正记录。”

speaker: Unknown
en: When you do that, I think more than often, more often than not, you come off as just looking defensive and you start obsessing over things that you don't actually have control over, which is what another person thinks of you.
zh: 当你那样做时，我认为通常，往往比你想象的更常，你会看起来只是在防御，并且你开始痴迷于那些你实际上无法控制的事情，那就是另一个人对你的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't even necessarily have that information.
zh: 你甚至不一定拥有那个信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I always ask myself in these moments, what is one thing that I can do, small, that will demonstrate the opposite of what I'm afraid this person thinks of me?
zh: 所以我总是在这些时刻问自己，我能做的一件小事是什么，它将演示出与我所担心的这个人对我的看法相反的东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I'll give you an example of this.
zh: 所以我会给你一个关于这方面的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was in a meeting a while ago, and we were talking about different things that we wanted to start tracking in the Whoop Journal.
zh: 一段时间以前我在开会，我们在谈论我们想要开始在 Whoop Journal 里追踪的不同事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And our chief technology officer suggested ketamine tracking.
zh: 我们的首席技术官提议追踪氯胺酮。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I thought she was making a joke and I laughed, and she looked at me very seriously and was like, "This isn't funny, Hilary.
zh: 我以为她在开玩笑，所以我笑了，她非常严肃地看着我，好像在说，“这不好笑，Hilary。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a serious issue for a lot of people, and it's an emerging problem in some cases.
zh: 这对很多人来说是个严重的问题，在某些情况下它是一个新兴的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we should take it seriously.
zh: 我认为我们应该认真对待它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's a lot of value we could provide here."
zh: 我认为我们可以在这里提供很多价值。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was completely humiliated.
zh: 我感到完全蒙羞。

speaker: Unknown
en: Humiliated because I actually take this stuff really seriously.
zh: 羞耻是因为我实际上真的很认真对待这些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I take addiction really seriously.
zh: 我非常认真地对待成瘾问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have a ton of empathy for people who struggle with it.
zh: 我对与之挣扎的人充满同情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I also think of myself as somebody who embraces new ideas and wants to be on the forefront and would never laugh off something that seems like a fringe issue that's I think becoming actually more and more a big part of what's happening today.
zh: 而且我也把自己看作是一个拥抱新想法并想站在前沿的人，绝不会嘲笑那些看起来像边缘问题的事情，我认为这实际上正越来越成为今天发生的事情的重要组成部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I realized that in that moment I was having that reaction because of the feeling that it gave me about who I am as a person, and I became so worried that this other person had the wrong impression of me.
zh: 所以我意识到，在那一刻我有那种反应是因为那种感觉给了我关于我是谁的感觉，我开始如此担心这个另人对我的错误印象。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I wanted to follow up with her after and say, "Let me explain myself.
zh: 我想事后跟进她说，“让我解释一下我自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me explain why I didn't mean that," or whatever it is.
zh: 让我解释一下为什么我不是那个意思，”或者不管是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as I said, I think usually you're fighting a losing battle when you're trying to do that, and it draws attention to the thing that you did poorly.
zh: 但是正如我所说，我认为通常当你在试图那样做时，你在打一场注定失败的仗，而且这会把注意力吸引到你做得糟糕的事情上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you don't really want to draw more attention to it.
zh: 而你并不真的想吸引更多的注意力到它上面。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want to move on, take action, move forward.
zh: 你想继续前进，采取行动，向前看。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I thought about, well, what am I afraid that she thinks of me?
zh: 所以我想，好吧，我担心她怎么看我？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm afraid that she thinks that maybe I don't take some of these health issues seriously.
zh: 我担心她认为也许我不认真对待这些健康问题中的一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm afraid she thinks that maybe I'm somebody who laughs off emerging trends.
zh: 我担心她认为也许我是那种嘲笑新兴趋势的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I thought about what's something that I could do to demonstrate the opposite of that?
zh: 所以我想到了我能做什么来演示相反的情况？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I did some research very, very quickly on what are some emerging public health concerns that people really aren't talking about that would be interesting to track?
zh: 我非常、非常快速地做了一些研究，看有哪些人们真的没有在谈论的新兴公共卫生问题会很有趣去追踪？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I found some interesting research about sports betting, and especially young people in sports betting, and it's becoming this thing that a lot of public health experts are very worried about.
zh: 我发现了一些关于体育博彩的有趣研究，特别是年轻人的体育博彩，这正在成为很多公共卫生专家非常担心的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I very quickly just sent her a note that said, "Wanted to build on this idea you had today.
zh: 所以我非常快速地给她发了一条信息说，“想在你今天的想法上做些补充。

speaker: Unknown
en: I really liked that idea, by the way.
zh: 我真的很喜欢那个主意，顺便说一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: I saw this article, I saw this research about this other emerging thing, sports betting, and I think it'd be really interesting for us to start tracking that because we could maybe draw some correlations between people stress.
zh: 我看到了这篇文章，我看到了关于这个其他新兴事物，体育博彩的研究，我认为我们将开始追踪它会非常有趣，因为也许我们可以得出一些与人们压力之间的相关性。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a stress monitor in Whoop.
zh: 我们在 Whoop 有一个压力监测器。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can track their stress.
zh: 我们可以追踪他们的压力。

speaker: Unknown
en: We could draw interesting correlations between betting behaviors and stress levels."
zh: 我们可以在投注行为和压力水平之间得出有趣的相关性。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's all I did.
zh: 所以这就是我所做的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: It took me five, 10 minutes total.
zh: 这花了我总共五到十分钟。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think it's a great example of showing this idea of counter-program that narrative, don't fight about the narrative.
zh: 但我认为这是演示这种反制叙事想法的一个很好的例子，而不是去争论那个叙事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when I teach this to my team, I'm always doing the same thing.
zh: 所以当我把这个教给我的团队时，我总是做同样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: They come to me.
zh: 他们来找我。

speaker: Unknown
en: They seem agitated about something and I say to them, "It seems like this is really bothering you.
zh: 他们看起来对某些事情感到焦躁，我对他们说，“看来这真的让你很困扰。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's going on in your head?
zh: 你脑子里在想什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you afraid of?
zh: 你害怕什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you worried about?"
zh: 你在担心什么？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And often it will emerge, "I'm worried that this other person thinks I'm bad at my job.
zh: 通常结果会是，“我担心这个另一个人觉得我不擅长我的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm worried that this person thinks I'm an idiot," whatever it is.
zh: “我担心这个人觉得我是个白痴，”不管是什么事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I challenge that.
zh: 然后我会反驳这种想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this is really important for managers too to challenge this negative thinking when you see it happen and not just validate it and allow them to go down these negative spirals.
zh: 我认为这对管理者来说也非常重要，当你看到这种情况时要反驳这种消极思维，而不仅仅是去认同它，任由他们陷入这些消极的螺旋中。

speaker: Unknown
en: I challenge it and I say, "First of all, I don't think there's evidence for that.
zh: 我会反驳它，我会说，“首先，我认为没有证据支持这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there evidence for that?
zh: 有证据支持这一点吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And even if there is, it doesn't really matter.
zh: 即使有，其实也没关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's something that you could do to show them that it's not true because you know it's not true?"
zh: 你能做些什么来向他们表明那不是真的，因为你知道那不是真的？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think giving people that power to focus on the next step they can take and the action that they can take that helps them feel more secure in their identity in who they are because their action demonstrates that, it just gets them out of that negative thinking and it gets them through that trough of despair that comes after you feel like you took a punch.
zh: 我认为给予人们这种力量去关注他们能采取的下一步，以及他们能采取的行动，这有助于他们在自己的身份和自我认同上感到更安全，因为他们的行动证明了这一点，这能让他们摆脱那种消极思维，并让他们度过那种在你感觉被打了一拳后随之而来的绝望低谷。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the idea here is when you're afraid somebody that matters in your career thinks ill of you, of something that you did, of you're not good at something or you think something that they're not happy about, this is a version of getting punched basically is you just feeling like someone thinks you're not doing a great job.
zh: 所以这里的想法是，当你害怕某个对你职业生涯很重要的人对你看法不好，对你做的一件事、你不擅长的某事，或者觉得他们对你做的事情不满意时，这基本上就是一种被打了一拳的版本，就是你感觉有人觉得你做得不够好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the tactic here is how to change their mind almost about you and give you something tangible to do.
zh: 所以这里的策略是如何改变他们对你的看法，并给你一些具体的事情去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 正是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the question to ask, and I wrote this down as you were talking, is, and this is what you ask of your reports, what is the one thing that you can do that demonstrates the opposite of what you think this person thinks about you?
zh: 所以要问的问题，我刚才把你说话的时候记下来了，就是，这也是你问你的下属的，你能做哪一件事来证明你认为这个人对你的看法是相反的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 正是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: This comes up all the time.
zh: 这种情况一直都在发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: There will be narratives that emerge, some are good, some are bad, about you and your career.
zh: 会出现一些叙事，有些是好的，有些是坏的，关于你和你的职业生涯。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think especially when people get to a place where they're putting themselves out there more, they're talking in more presentations, they're talking in more meetings, it's very natural for them to become concerned with the perception themselves.
zh: 我认为特别是当人们到了一个开始更多地展示自己的阶段，他们在更多的演讲中发言，在更多的会议中发言，他们开始关注别人对自己的看法是非常自然的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it is scary because it feels like something, as I said, you don't have control over.
zh: 这是很可怕的，因为正如我所说，感觉像是有些事情你无法控制。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so exactly.
zh: 所以确实是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: If instead of focusing people around what do these people think of me, you focus them around, well, what are you going to do next to demonstrate that you are the person that you know yourself to be, I think that can just be incredibly effective at giving people more of a sense of agency.
zh: 如果不是让人们关注这些人怎么看我，而是让他们关注，好吧，你下一步要做什么来证明你就是你所知道的自己，我认为这可以在给予人们更多主观能动性方面非常有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess talk about the balance of I'm just going to prove everyone wrong against what they think versus here's who I am and I know this is me and this person is mistaken.
zh: 我想讨论一下平衡，一种是我就是要证明每个人都错了，反驳他们的想法，另一种是这就是我，我知道这就是我，而这个人是误会了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And instead of debating them, I'm going to show them who I am.
zh: 而不是去和他们辩论，我要向他们展示我是谁。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just not overstressing about everyone thinking things about you in different ways.
zh: 只是对每个人以不同方式看待你这件事不要过度焦虑。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is some value I think in having a little bit of a chip on your shoulder.
zh: 我认为有点想证明自己是对的还是有一些价值的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You see that people who are really successful, they do have a little bit of like, "I'm going to prove them wrong."
zh: 你会发现那些真正成功的人，他们确实有一点那种，“我要证明他们是错的”的心态。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I don't want to say that you shouldn't think about it at all or you shouldn't care.
zh: 所以我不想说你根本不应该去想它，或者你不应该在乎。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course, it's natural to care, and of course, it's fine to care, but I do want to just help my team build this habit of doing the things that you know to be right and having conviction in that.
zh: 当然，在乎是很自然的，当然，在乎也没关系，但我确实想帮助我的团队建立这种做你知道正确的事情的习惯，并对此有坚定的信念。

speaker: Unknown
en: Being open to learning along the way and calibrating as you go, but not becoming overly concerned with your fears of what other people are going to think of you.
zh: 在过程中保持开放的学习态度并在过程中进行校准，但不要过度担心你会对别人怎么想你的恐惧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I think especially for otherwise really thoughtful, really the people who are hard on themselves, I think that that just holds them back from being the person that they can be.
zh: 因为我认为特别是对于那些原本非常深思熟虑、对自己非常严格的人来说，我认为这只是阻碍了他们成为他们能够成为的那个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a key part of this is, this is going to help you stop just spiraling on thinking about what they think about you and gives you something to do that will change that.
zh: 所以这里的关键部分是，这将帮助你停止只是在纠结他们怎么想你，并给你做一些事情来改变这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the other key point here is don't try to convince them otherwise.
zh: 然后这里另一个关键点是不要试图去说服他们让他们改变想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're not going to go to your manager like, "Oh, I really think ketamine therapy and addiction is really important, and I didn't mean to say it this way," and that kind of thing.
zh: 你不会去找你的经理说，“哦，我真的认为氯胺酮疗法和成瘾非常重要，我不是故意这样说的，”以及诸如此类的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not interested in litigating the things that happened already when we can move forward.
zh: 我不想去争论那些已经发生的事情，既然我们可以向前看。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm certainly not interested in litigating what another person thinks about a thing that happened.
zh: 我当然也不想对别人对某件已发生事情的看法进行争论。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like I've spent so much time talking to people in meetings, whatever it is, where it's just this ruminating on something that has already happened.
zh: 我觉得我在会议上花了这么多时间和人交谈，不管是什么事，都只是在对已经发生的事情进行反刍。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very anxious thinking pattern, I think, and people can just get stuck in it.
zh: 我认为这是一种非常焦虑的思维模式，人们可能会陷入其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so let them do it.
zh: 所以就让他们去做吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like when you get bad feedback or critical feedback and you naturally have this reaction of, "Oh, well, that's not fair because they don't understand.
zh: 就像当你得到糟糕的反馈或批评性的反馈时，你自然会有这种反应，“哦，那不公平，因为他们不理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: I actually have numbers I have to deliver on, or I only had 10 minutes to do this, so of course, it wasn't perfect."
zh: 我实际上有必须要交付的数字，或者我只有 10 分钟来做这件事，所以当然它不完美。”

speaker: Unknown
en: You naturally come up with these reasons why you are actually not wrong, and that's fine.
zh: 你自然地会想出这些理由说明你其实没错，这没关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't want to say you should feel bad for doing that.
zh: 我不想说你应该为此感觉不好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let yourself have the pity party, let yourself feel those things, but then you got to move on as quickly as possible because those feelings, they actually do tend to spiral and get worse if you're not actively working against them.
zh: 让自己举办一场自怜派对，让自己去感受这些情绪，但然后你必须尽快地继续前进，因为这些情绪，如果你不主动地对抗它们，它们确实往往会螺旋式恶化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oftentimes these sorts of lessons come from the person experiencing this themselves.
zh: 通常这类教训来自于亲身体验的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is this something that you dealt with when you're starting your career or even now?
zh: 这是你在职业生涯刚开始时甚至现在遇到过的事情吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, absolutely, 100%.
zh: 哦，绝对是，百分之百。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it is more than just my career, but just my general mental health and my life.
zh: 我认为这不仅仅是在我的职业生涯中，而是我的整体心理健康和我的生活中。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of where this comes from is a concept in cognitive behavioral therapy called behavioral activation.
zh: 这里的很多内容来自于认知行为疗法中一个称为行为激活的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in my former job, I was working for a company called Big Health and we make digital therapeutics.
zh: 在我以前的工作中，我在一家名为 Big Health 的公司工作，我们制作数字疗法。

speaker: Unknown
en: So those are mobile apps that have been clinically validated to treat behavioral conditions like insomnia, depression, anxiety.
zh: 所以这些是经过临床验证的用于治疗行为状况的移动应用程序，比如失眠症、抑郁症、焦虑症。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was working on a new depression therapeutic, and so went very deep on this and was working with a really wonderful clinical team full of clinical psychologists who helped me understand the techniques that therapists use when they are working with people who have depression.
zh: 我当时正在研发一种新的抑郁症疗法，所以我对此进行了深入的研究，并与一个非常棒的临床团队合作，团队里有很多临床心理学家，他们帮助我理解了治疗师在治疗抑郁症患者时使用的技巧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so much of depression is characterized by these negative thinking patterns and this feeling that I feel bad and I just need to wait until I feel better, and then I'll start doing the things that are good for me.
zh: 抑郁的很大特征是这些消极的思维模式，以及这种我感觉很糟，我只需要等待直到我感觉好起来，然后我才会开始做对我有利的事情的感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't feel like responding to this text, so I'm just not going to do it, but I'll respond when I feel better.
zh: 我不想回复这条短信，所以我就不回，但我会等我感觉好点的时候再回。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't feel like working out, so I'm not going to do it, but I'll do it when I feel better.
zh: 我不想去锻炼，所以我就不去，但我会等我感觉好点的时候再去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the truth is that doesn't go away on its own, especially if you have depression.
zh: 而事实是，这不会自行消失，尤其是如果你患有抑郁症的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, the idea of behavioral activation is you have to identify these actions that you can take that will reverse that negative spiral and will improve your mood.
zh: 同样，行为激活的理念是你必须识别你可以采取的这些行动，这些行动将扭转那种消极的螺旋并将改善你的情绪。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the misconception is I'll feel better and then I'll act.
zh: 所以误解是，我会感觉好起来，然后我会行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the thing that therapists try to teach people, they're working with them in therapy is I will act and then I will feel better.
zh: 而治疗师试图教导人们的事情，当他们在治疗中与人们合作时是，我会行动，然后我会感觉好起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: But acting is hard if you are in the furrows of depression.
zh: 但是如果你处于抑郁的沟壑中，行动是很难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so easier said than done.
zh: 所以说是容易做起来难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of the work is in how you help people identify specific actions that they can take that will reliably lift their mood.
zh: 很多工作在于你如何帮助人们识别他们可以采取的具体行动，这些行动将可靠地提升他们的情绪。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I have a list of myself.
zh: 我的意思是，我自己有一个清单。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've got a list on my phone of my behavioral activations, and it's things that I know I can do if I start feeling like the walls are closing around me, if I feel myself getting sucked into very low mood or negative thinking, or whatever it is.
zh: 我的手机里有一个我的行为激活清单，上面列着我知道我可以做的事情，如果我开始感觉周围的墙壁正在逼近，如果我感觉自己被吸入非常低落的情绪或消极的思考，或者不管是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can see how effective that is at just getting you out of there versus the instinct to just go and lay in bed and feel bad for yourself, which I understand very well.
zh: 你能看到这在让你摆脱那种状态方面是多么有效，相比之下那种直接去躺在床上自怜自艾的本能，这一点我非常理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so understanding that concept, which is at its core a therapeutic concept used in cognitive behavioral therapy, but it changed how I see the entire world and how I see, especially as a manager, the ways that people on my team think and behave and how easy it is to get stuck in some of these downward spirals that you really need to actively push back on.
zh: 因此理解那个概念，其核心是一个在认知行为疗法中使用的治疗概念，但它改变了我看待整个世界的方式，以及作为管理者我如何看待团队成员的思维和行为方式，以及陷入这些你需要主动反击的下行螺旋是多么容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as a manager, I want to help them do that.
zh: 作为管理者，我想帮助他们做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to help them, A, see that, see the ways they are in some ways sabotaging themselves, getting in their own ways with whatever is going on in their head.
zh: 我想帮助他们，A，看到这一点，看到他们在某些方面如何破坏自己，被脑子里发生的任何事情所阻碍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I want to help them counter-program it in themselves.
zh: 然后我想帮助他们在自己内心进行反向编程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also, as I said, counter-program the things that you are worried about out there as well.
zh: 而且，正如我所说，也对你担心的外界事物进行反向编程。

speaker: Unknown
en: So interesting.
zh: 太有意思了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the core of this technique is what's an action, and you said this, it could be very small.
zh: 所以这个技巧的核心是什么是一个行动，你说过，它可能非常小。

speaker: Unknown
en: Very small.
zh: 非常小。

speaker: Unknown
en: That you can take that in this case shows someone else you're not who they think you are.
zh: 你可以采取的行动，在这种情况下向别人表明你不是他们认为的那种人。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 你担心他们以某种方式看待你，你想采取一个行动帮助他们看到你不是那样。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 是的，这就是「承受打击」的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: So behavioral activation just conceptually is, how are you taking action to reverse the downward feeling or the negative feeling that you're feeling?
zh: 所以行为激活在概念上就是，你如何采取行动来扭转你感觉到的下行感觉或消极感觉？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the take a punch concept is that applied in the context of I'm in a working environment.
zh: 而「承受打击」的概念是在工作环境中应用了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am very conscious of how I'm being perceived by other people.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 这给我带来了巨大的压力。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think especially for product people who are... So much of their self identity is wrapped up in having the answers, being competent, getting things done.
zh: 我认为特别是对于那些产品人员来说，他们的自我认同很大程度上与拥有答案、表现出能力、把事情做完联系在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so many of them have been people who have been really good at that for most of their careers, which is how they got into these jobs in the first place.
zh: 他们中的许多人在职业生涯的大部分时间里都非常擅长这一点，这也是他们首先获得这些工作的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that can be an extremely stressful thing for them.
zh: 我认为这对他们来说可能是一件非常有压力的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: That in many cases can be the driver of burnout and the driver of I can't really handle the stress of this job anymore.
zh: 在很多情况下，这可能是职业倦怠的驱动因素，也是我再也无法处理这份工作的压力的驱动因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think the take a punch concept is more just applied to that specific problem of I'm struggling at work and I'm struggling largely because of my perceptions of other people and I want to feel more agency in that situation.
zh: 所以我认为「承受打击」的概念更多地是应用于我正在工作中挣扎这个特定问题，而我很大程度上是因为对别人的看法而挣扎，我想在那个情况下感觉到更多的主观能动性。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is so cool.
zh: 这太酷了。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the idea of the specific take a punch concept, what kind of impact have you seen this have on people's mood and careers?
zh: 关于具体的「承受打击」概念，你看到这对人们的情绪和职业生涯有什么样的影响？

speaker: Unknown
en: How big a deal is this specific tactic?
zh: 这个具体策略有多大影响力？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I think it's a big deal on two levels.
zh: 嗯，我认为它在两个层面上都很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: One, it's a big deal because it can help you in a crisis or a minor crisis.
zh: 第一，它很重要是因为它可以在危机或轻微危机中帮助你。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I actually think it's a bigger deal because I see so many people who don't put themselves out there because they're afraid of how it's going to go.
zh: 但我实际上认为它更重要，因为我看到很多人不把自己暴露出来，因为他们害怕结果会如何。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think of the classic example of I'm often trying to encourage people to speak up in meetings more, to practice the skill of how you move a conversation forward in a way that can contribute value, both because doing so I think is important because nobody wants to be in bad meetings, but also because it will help with your career.
zh: 所以我想到了那个典型的例子，我经常试图鼓励人们在会议上多发言，练习如何以一种能贡献价值的方式推动对话的技巧，既是因为这样做很重要，因为没有人想参加糟糕的会议，也是因为它对你的职业生涯有帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is how you get on people's radar as somebody who's like, "Oh, that person's got great ideas, thinks about things the right way," whatever it is.
zh: 这就是让你进入人们视野的方法，作为一个像「噢，那个人有很棒的想法，以正确的方式思考事情」之类的人，不管是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's one of these things that I talk to people about it and they are interested in coming to the meeting and hearing about these big decisions are getting made, but they just want to sit there and observe.
zh: 我认为这是我和人们谈论的一件事，他们有兴趣参加会议并听到这些重大决策的制定，但他们只想坐在那里观察。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, first of all, every additional person in a meeting has a cost, because every additional person in a meeting makes the people in that meeting less candid than they would have been if there were fewer people in that meeting.
zh: 而我会说，首先，会议中的每一个额外人员都有成本，因为会议中的每一个额外人员都会使会议中的人们不如人少时那么坦诚。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so one key piece of a meeting is you usually have a problem you're trying to solve collectively as a group.
zh: 所以会议的一个关键部分是你通常有一个你们试图作为一个集体解决的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's really hard to do that if people are being overly cautious about what they're saying because there's too many people in there.
zh: 如果人们对自己说的话过于谨慎，因为里面的人太多了，那么真的很难做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when I tell people this, I'm like, "It's really important that you earn your place in this meeting and let's work on how to do that."
zh: 所以当我告诉人们这一点时，我会说，「在这个会议上赢得你的一席之地真的很重要，让我们一起来研究如何做到这一点。」

speaker: Unknown
en: And the core piece of that is you've got to say stuff that's valuable.
zh: 而其中的核心部分是你必须说出有价值的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And people always come up with all these excuses for why they can't do it.
zh: 人们总是想出各种各样的借口来解释为什么他们做不到。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one thing I've learned is that I think people are really good at coming up with very rational sounding reasons to not do things that just make them uncomfortable.
zh: 我学到了一件事，我认为人们非常擅长为不做那些让他们感到不舒服的事情，找听起来非常合理的理由。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in their head they're like, "Oh no, I'm too junior.
zh: 但在他们脑子里他们会想，“噢不，我太资浅了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody wants to hear what I have to say.
zh: 没人想听我要说的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or everyone was already thinking it.
zh: 或者大家也都已经这么想了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or I like to process things internally.
zh: 或者我喜欢在内部处理事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the time I say them, the conversation moved on," whatever it is.
zh: 等到我说出来的时候，对话已经继续向前了，”不管是什么理由。

speaker: Unknown
en: So much of that skill, it's like a communication skill at its core, it's just how to express yourself verbally, but so much of the blocker of that is I think fear.
zh: 这种技能很大程度上，它核心上是一种沟通技能，只是如何口头表达你自己，但阻碍它的很大一部分我认为是恐惧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fear of saying the wrong thing.
zh: 害怕说错话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fear of looking stupid.
zh: 害怕看起来很蠢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fear of just the discomfort of everyone in a room turning and looking at you as you're trying to formulate a half-baked thought.
zh: 害怕那种当房间里的所有人都转过身看着你、而你正试图组织一个半成熟的想法时的不适感。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you can help people be less afraid of that, that's 90% of the challenge of actually improving some of these skills.
zh: 所以如果你能帮助人们减少对那件事的恐惧，那就是实际提升这些技能的 90% 的挑战所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think when you give people the skills of taking a punch, you are helping them feel less afraid of getting the punch in the first place.
zh: 所以我认为当你给了人们挨打的能力，你是在帮助他们从一开始就不那么害怕挨打。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's why I think it's so important.
zh: 这就是为什么我认为这如此重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's profound, the second order effect of the skill.
zh: 这很深刻，这种技能的二阶效应。

zh: 噢，我认为这是我的激进观点。

en: You hear people talking about craft and taste and product management, and it's all very wonderful.
zh: 你听到人们谈论手艺和品味以及产品管理，这一切都很美好。

en: And I'm totally on board.
zh: 我完全赞同。

zh: 我对那种事情很着迷，但是我会想，好吧，如果你真的纯粹是为了对这项游戏的热爱，你只是热爱产品管理，你为什么要为和你完全一样的人、在一个向其他公司销售且不用担心定价的公司里构建产品？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no real... I mean, I don't want to act like I think this is easy, to be clear.
zh: 没有真正的……我的意思是，我不想表现得好像我认为这很容易，明确地说。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in the grand scheme of things, I wish that the people who have this pure love of product management and have this pure love of building things that you would see more of that applied to building for low income people, building for social services, things like that, that really, really need that kind of work.
zh: 但从大局来看，我希望那些对产品管理有纯粹热爱、对构建事物有纯粹热爱的人，你能看到更多这种热情被应用于为低收入人群构建，为公共服务构建，像这样真正、真正需要这种工作的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there's a level of prestige obviously associated with working in certain companies, and you get less of that in other industries.
zh: 我认为显然在特定公司工作有一定程度的声望，而在其他行业你会得到的较少。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so people would naturally gravitate toward that.
zh: 所以人们自然会倾向于那个。

en: I totally get it.
zh: 我完全理解。

en: I totally get it.

en: You get paid better.

zh: 我要说的是，我知道那里有很多人。

en: I know there's a ton of people out there doing really, really important work in really, really hard spaces, and I see you and I appreciate it and shout out to you.
zh: 我知道有很多人在非常、非常困难的领域做着非常、非常重要的 工作，我看到你们了，我很感激，向你们致意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Awesome.

speaker: Unknown

en: I think this will resonate with a lot of people.
zh: 我认为这会引起很多人的共鸣。

en: I want to move on to another trait/habits/skill that you are good at and help people learn, which is being very transparent in what's happening within the organization, within your thinking.
zh: 我想转到你擅长的另一个特质/习惯/技能，也就是非常透明地对待组织内部发生的事情以及你自己的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: You almost help people think the way you think and see the way you think so that they can operate at a higher level.
zh: 你几乎是在帮助人们像你一样思考，像你一样看待，以便他们能在更高的层面上运作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just talk about that, what that looks like and why that's important.
zh: 就谈谈那是什么样子的，以及为什么那很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's interesting, I think another thing I hear a lot of people complain about in organizations is the why do 10 people have to sign off on this email before I send it kind of problem.
zh: 很有趣，我认为我听到很多人在组织中抱怨的另一件事是，为什么我发送这封邮件之前必须有 10 个人签字这类问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the answer to that is because those 10 people all have different information, different context, and in many cases, completely different working models for how the CEO of the company and other strategic leaders in the company think.
zh: 我认为答案在于，那 10 个人都有不同的信息，不同的上下文，而且在很多情况下，对于公司的 CEO 和公司的其他战略领导人是如何思考的，有着完全不同的工作模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it makes things super inefficient.
zh: 这让事情超级低效。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think people will often say like, "Oh, it's a process problem."
zh: 我认为人们经常会说，“噢，这是一个流程问题。”

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not a process problem.
zh: 这不是流程问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not approval problem.
zh: 这不是审批问题。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我认为这是一个透明度和沟通问题，比如向下的沟通，向外的沟通。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I mean by that is when I think about artifact-based communication, so reading a strategy document for...
zh: 我的意思是，当我考虑到基于制品的沟通时，所以阅读一份战略文档，关于……

speaker: Unknown
en: About artifact-based communication.
zh: 关于基于制品的沟通。

speaker: Unknown
en: So reading a strategy document, for example.
zh: 所以阅读一份战略文档，例如。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone at the company reads the strategy document.
zh: 公司里的每个人都阅读那份战略文档。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great.
zh: 很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone is working from the same idea of what the strategy is.
zh: 每个人都基于对战略是什么的同一个认知来工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then things change, right?
zh: 但随后事情会发生变化，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Especially if you're working in a really dynamic space, new competitive threats emerge, new opportunities emerge all the time.
zh: 特别是如果你在一个非常动态的领域工作，新的竞争威胁会出现，新的机会会一直出现。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is especially true now with AI.
zh: 这一点现在在 AI 方面尤为真实。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously everyone is lighting their strategies on fire and trying to figure out the best way to sort of transform their organization.
zh: 显然，每个人都在点燃他们的战略，并试图找出改造其组织的最佳方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if the way that you understand what's going on at the company is from reading a document that was written six months ago, you're going to be working from outdated information and you're not going to be able to think and respond to new things that happen.
zh: 因此，如果你了解公司正在发生事情的方式是阅读一份六个月前写成的文档，你将基于过时的信息工作，而且你将无法思考并应对发生的新事物。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what is much more helpful than understanding what your CEO thinks is, I think understanding how your CEO thinks.
zh: 所以，比理解你的 CEO 认为什么更有帮助的是，我认为理解你的 CEO 是如何思考的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that goes for all sorts of levels of the company.
zh: 这适用于公司的所有层级。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to understand how all the strategic leaders at my company think, and I want my team to understand how I think.
zh: 我想理解我公司的所有战略领导者是如何思考的，我也希望我的团队理解我是如何思考的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when I feel confident that people on my team understand how I think, I don't need to read their emails, I don't need to approve things.
zh: 当我对我的团队理解我是如何思考的有信心时，我不需要阅读他们的电子邮件，我不需要批准事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: The times where I feel like I need to do that is because I'm working with people where I'm like, I don't have confidence that these people understand how I think, or I don't have confidence that they understand how this email or whatever it is, is going to be received by this important person.
zh: 我觉得我需要那样做的时候，是因为我在与这样的人一起工作，我觉得我对这些人理解我是如何思考的没有信心，或者我对他们理解这封邮件或其他什么东西会被这位重要人物如何看待没有信心。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I try to teach that to my team.
zh: 所以我试着把这教给我的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the way that I do that is a few ways.
zh: 我做这件事的方式有几种。

speaker: Unknown
en: First, I'm in meetings with people, important people at the company.
zh: 首先，我和人们在一起开会，公司里重要的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm constantly hearing the things that they're saying and paying attention to sort of the note behind the note.
zh: 所以我不断地听到他们正在说的话，并注意那些弦外之音。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why do I think they're saying this?
zh: 为什么我认为他们在说这个？

speaker: Unknown
en: What insight do they have that they're bringing to this conversation that might not be obvious?
zh: 他们有什么洞见带到这次对话中，而这些可能不是显而易见的？ [[320]】 而且我试着每周都为此努力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I try to make an effort every week.
zh: 我每周都会努力。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't always do it, but I try to send my team just a quick rundown in Slack of, "Here are the most important conversations or the most interesting conversations I had this week.
zh: 我不总是能做到，但我试着给我的团队在 Slack 上发一个简短的简报，“这是我这周最重要的对话或最有趣的对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's what that person said verbatim."
zh: 那个人逐字说了什么。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, I write a lot of notes so I've got it.
zh: 同样，我写很多笔记，所以我都有。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you've got a transcriber, maybe that'll help you.
zh: 如果你有一个转录员，也许那会帮到你。

speaker: Unknown
en: "And here's what I interpret that as.
zh: “而这是我对它的解读。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's why I think they say that.
zh: 这就是为什么我认为他们那么说。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's where I think that's coming from and here's what I'm going to do differently as a result."
zh: 这就是我认为这来源于哪里，以及因此我将会有什么不同的做法。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And these aren't long.
zh: 而这些并不长。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes if I don't have time, I'll just, in a team meeting, I'll literally just go through my notes from the week and sort of voiceover stuff and editorialize it as I go.
zh: 有时候如果我没有时间，我会在团队会议中，真的只是过一遍我这一周的笔记，并且对内容进行旁白解说和评论。

speaker: Unknown
en: And over time, I think my team has a pretty good sense of what people are saying and how to think about the thinking behind it and how this person thinks, how this person thinks and how I think.
zh: 随着时间的推移，我认为我的团队对人们在说什么以及如何思考其背后的思考，以及这个人如何思考，那个人如何思考，以及我如何思考，有了相当好的感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think when you get an entire organization working that way where everyone's working from the same models of what the CEO thinks matters, what level of risk tolerance the company has, things like that, then you can actually start to move much, much faster and communication becomes much, much, much less painful.
zh: 我认为当你让整个组织以这种方式工作时，每个人都基于关于 CEO 认为什么重要、公司有什么样的风险承受能力等事情的相同模型工作，那么你实际上可以开始更快、更快地行动，沟通也会变得痛苦少得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the tactic here is to help your teams kind of build a mental model of everyone in the company that matters so that it's... The way you put it almost is when they're emailing them or asking for something, they already know how they're going to respond.
zh: 所以这里的战术是帮助你的团队建立公司里每个重要人物的心理模型，这样它就是……你表达它的方式几乎是，当他们在给他们发电子邮件或请求某事时，他们已经知道他们会如何回应。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is they're an example you could share of something like this, of just something a person at Whoop of how they think?
zh: 有没有一个你可以分享的关于这类事情的例子，关于 Whoop 的某一个人是如何思考的？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know, maybe you could keep it anonymous just to make this a little reel of the kind of mental model you might want to build around someone.
zh: 我不知道，也许你可以保持匿名，只是为了对你可能想要围绕某人建立的这种心理模型做一个摘要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So our CEO, Will, is somebody who obsesses over pixels in a way that is challenging to get things through design review, but I think results in a product that is a thousand times better than it would be if he were accepting of small excuses here and there for, "Oh, well this, we had to cut scope here.
zh: 所以我们的 CEO，Will，是一个痴迷于像素的人，以至于很难通过设计审查，但我认为这导致产品比他在这里那里接受小借口要好上一千倍，比如，“噢，好吧，这个，我们不得不在这里削减范围。

speaker: Unknown
en: We couldn't quite do what they wanted here."
zh: 我们在这里无法完全做他们想要的。”

speaker: Unknown
en: He sets a high bar and he holds it and he doesn't compromise.
zh: 他设定了高标准并保持它，而且他不妥协。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think this can sometimes get misconstrued, and I think a lot of people might think that he just wants maximal scope on everything.
zh: 我认为这有时会被误解，我认为很多人可能认为他只是想在所有事情上都要最大的范围。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that is a misunderstanding of what he cares about.
zh: 我认为这是对他关心什么的误解。

speaker: Unknown
en: We often get feedback from him that's like, "This doesn't feel like the future and everything that we're building needs to feel like the future."
zh: 我们经常从他那里得到反馈，比如，“这感觉不像未来，而我们构建的每样东西都需要感觉像未来。”

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of people hear that and they're kind of like, "Oh gosh, we're never going to get this thing done on time.
zh: 很多人听到那个然后想，“天哪，我们永远无法按时完成这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can't make any sort of sacrifices to scope or anything like that."
zh: 我们不能对范围做任何牺牲或任何类似的事情。”

speaker: Unknown
en: But when I hear that, what I hear is more that we have this AI coach in the product, we have all this amazing data in the product.
zh: 但当我听到那个时，我听到更多的是我们要在这个产品中有这个 AI 教练，我们在这个产品中有所有这些惊人的数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're tracking every single one of your heartbeats and we're pulling at all this other data and we have every screen is a moment to show that to people in a way that feels like something that has never existed before.
zh: 我们正在追踪你的每一次心跳，我们正在拉取所有其他数据，而且我们有每一个屏幕都是向人们展示这一点的时刻，以一种感觉像以前从未存在过的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are small ways to do that, right?
zh: 而且有一些小的方法可以做到这一点，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like how you pull in.
zh: 就像你如何引入。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're explaining a concept like VO2 Max, which is a measure of your cardiovascular health, you can explain that to people with static content or you can explain that to people by bringing their data into the method of explanation that you're using.
zh: 如果你在解释一个像 VO2 Max 这样的概念，它是你心血管健康的衡量标准，你可以用静态内容向人们解释那个，或者你可以通过把他们的数据带入你正在使用的解释方法来向人们解释那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can make it really conversational because you're using this AI coach.
zh: 你可以让它真的非常对话式，因为你正在使用这个 AI 教练。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can make it feel more like you're talking to a person and a person who by the way has all the data about you, which doesn't exist today.
zh: 你可以让它感觉更像你在和一个人交谈，顺便说一句，这个人拥有关于你的所有数据，而这在今天是不存在的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your doctor doesn't have that, your coach doesn't have that.
zh: 你的医生没有那个，你的教练也没有那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's not like, "Oh gosh, we've got to blow up the scope on this thing and make it a hundred X as big."
zh: 这并不是说，“天哪，我们必须把这个事情的范围搞大，让它变大一百倍。”

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's finding these little touches to say, "Wow, that was really magical, that was really thoughtful and this feels like the future.
zh: 而是找到这些细微的触点，以此来说，“哇，那真的很神奇，那真的很周到，这感觉像是未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: This feels like I'm very conscious of the fact that this product knows so much about me and is able to sort out the signal from the noise on that in these really small and elegant ways."
zh: 这种感觉就像是我非常清楚地意识到，这个产品非常了解我，并且能够通过这些非常微小和优雅的方式，从中分辨出信号和噪音。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for something like that, I would get that feedback in design review or I'd hear that in a design review and maybe one of my PMs would be in that design review.
zh: 所以对于类似这样的事情，我会在设计评审中得到那种反馈，或者我会在设计评审中听到那个，也许我的某个产品经理也会在那个设计评审中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I bring that to the team.
zh: 所以我把那个带给团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I hear of things like that in a few different design reviews.
zh: 我在几个不同的设计评审中听到了类似的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I bring those back to the team and I'm like, "I've noticed that recently we are consistently getting this type of feedback.
zh: 所以我把这些带回给团队，我是说，“我注意到最近我们一直收到这种类型的反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's why I think it's really important to Will, because I think he's really focused on building the health company of the future.
zh: 以下是我认为这对 Will 至关重要的原因，因为我认为他真的专注于建立未来的健康公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't want you all to think that this just means we have to just throw AI at everything and we have to just throw maximum scope at everything.
zh: 我不希望你们大家认为这意味着我们必须只是把 AI 扔到所有事情上，我们必须只是把最大的范围扔到所有事情上。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the key is understanding on the matrix of cost and effort for impact, what are those high impact but low cost ways that we can just find and sprinkle through the experience and really try to make that magical?"
zh: 我认为关键是在成本和付出对影响的关系矩阵上理解，什么是那些我们能够找到并散布在体验中的高影响但低成本的方式，并真正尝试使其变得神奇？”

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm connecting the dots for my team.
zh: 所以我在为我的团队串联这些点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm saying, "You weren't in all these meetings, but I saw it.
zh: 我是说，“你们没有参加所有这些会议，但我看到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's what I heard.
zh: 这就是我听到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's my interpretation of what I heard, and here's how I'm thinking about how this other person thinks about it.
zh: 这就是我对听到的内容的解读，这也是我在思考另一个人是如何思考它的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so as a result, here are some things that I think we can do across our product going forward."
zh: 因此，以下是我认为我们在未来的产品中可以做的事情。”

speaker: Lenny
en: Essentially these are principles, values, or tenets per person of what matters to them.
zh: 本质上，这些是每个人关于什么对他们很重要的原则、价值观或宗旨。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 正是。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for Nick it's, "This needs to feel like we're living in the future."
zh: 所以对于 Nick 来说，这是“这需要感觉像是我们生活在未来。”

speaker: Unknown
en: It can't just be like another heartbeat dragging out.
zh: 它不能只是像另一个心跳拖出来那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is so cool.
zh: 这太酷了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's so many trickle-down benefit to this.
zh: 这有很多 trickle-down 好处。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is people feel like they're aware of what's happening.
zh: 一个是人们感觉他们知道正在发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's one of the most common, I think, piece of feedback people have with big companies.
zh: 我认为这是人们对大公司最常见的反馈之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, "I don't know what's happening."
zh: 比如，“我不知道正在发生什么。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's so much visibility to all the secretive stuff happening in the meetings.
zh: 所以对所有会议中发生的秘密事情有如此多的可见性。

speaker: Unknown
en: "I don't know what people are deciding my fates and all these discussions."
zh: “我不知道是谁在决定我的命运，以及所有这些讨论。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think just even knowing that you're sharing all this is so powerful.
zh: 所以我认为即使只是知道你正在分享所有这些也是非常强大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, and on that note, when I approach these conversations, I always try to think of them as, even if I don't agree with the feedback, if I don't agree with the decision, what is the insight that I'm missing?
zh: 嗯，而且在这个话题上，当我接近这些对话时，我总是试着把它们看作，即使我不同意这个反馈，即使我不同意这个决定，我错过的洞察是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: How am I wrong about this?
zh: 我在这方面哪里错了？

speaker: Unknown
en: In ways like, what would be true for this other person to be right?
zh: 在像这样的方式中，什么情况下会让这个其他人是正确的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'll go through that thought exercise and I might not get to the other side and agree with it.
zh: 我会经历那个思维练习，我可能不会到达另一边并同意它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I might still think I'm right or whatever.
zh: 我可能仍然认为我是对的或者无论什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: But oftentimes it forcing myself to think that way forces me to think about how this other person thinks it.
zh: 但通常情况下，强迫自己那样思考会强迫我去思考这个另一个人是如何思考它的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if I do that enough, I will be like, "Oh, this makes sense.
zh: 如果我那样做得足够多，我会像，“哦，这有道理。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this makes sense if.
zh: 我认为如果有……，这就有道理。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this makes sense if, and oh, maybe this other thing is true."
zh: 我认为如果有……，并且哦，也许这另外一件事是真的，这就有道理。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think when I hear the people, the people who are like, "I don't know what's going on with this company," I think they do the opposite.
zh: 而且我认为当我听到那些说，“我不知道这家公司发生了什么”的人时，我认为他们做的是相反的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think they look for reasons to disagree and they look for holes to poke in, "Well, this decision doesn't make any sense because I came up with something that might be wrong about it."
zh: 我认为他们寻找不同意的理由，他们寻找漏洞去戳穿，“嗯，这个决定没有任何意义，因为我想出了一个可能关于它是错误的事情。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's another thing, by the way, in terms of just sort of helping your team have the emotional maturity to exist and thrive in an organization is helping them think that way, helping them understand you have a point of view.
zh: 我认为这是另一件事，顺便说一句，在只是帮助你的团队获得情感成熟度以在一个组织中存在和茁壮成长方面，是帮助他们那样思考，帮助他们理解你有一个观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your point of view is important, but on some level, you do kind of have to have respect for these other points of view and have the humility to think that maybe they're onto something that you're not onto.
zh: 你的观点很重要，但在某种程度上，你确实必须尊重这些其他观点，并有谦卑去想也许他们正在接触一些你没有接触的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's amazing how much you can learn into it without having to have all the facts just by doing that.
zh: 你能从中学习到多少东西是惊人的，甚至不需要掌握所有事实，只要这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're like, "Well, this person's behavior makes sense in a situation where X, Y, and Z is happening," oftentimes you'll find that X, Y and Z is happening.
zh: 如果你像，“嗯，这个人的行为在 X、Y 和 Z 正在发生的情况下是有道理的，”通常你会发现 X、Y 和 Z 正在发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm glad you went there.
zh: 我很高兴你去了那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wanted to actually follow this thread, which is kind of a different direction, but I think a lot of people are always struggling with this as a leader.
zh: 我实际上想顺着这个话题，这有点不同的方向，但我认为很多人作为领导者总是在为此挣扎。

speaker: Unknown
en: When your leader disagree, it does say something that you completely disagree with, but you still need to represent that as, "Here's the thing we're doing."
zh: 当你的领导不同意，它确实说了一些你完全不同意的事情，但你仍然需要将其代表为“这就是我们要做的事情。”

speaker: Unknown
en: But you don't want to be like, "Oh, just because Nick said so."
zh: 但你不想像，“噢，就因为 Nick 这么说。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Because you lose power as a leader.
zh: 因为你会作为领导者丧失权力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there something you've learned about how to do that well when your leader tells you to do something you disagree with and you still need to get your team to do it.
zh: 当你的领导者让你去做一件你不同意的事情，而你仍然需要让你的团队去做时，关于如何把这件事做好，你有什么心得吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: First, I do try to go through the what if I'm wrong exercise.
zh: 首先，我确实尝试进行「如果我错了」的练习。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a lot of people just sort of expect that if you ask somebody a open-ended question like, "Why are we doing this?"
zh: 我认为很多人只是有种预期，如果你问某人一个开放式问题，比如「我们为什么要做这个？」

speaker: Unknown
en: You're going to get a straightforward answer.
zh: 你会得到一个直截了当的回答。

speaker: Unknown
en: And oftentimes the answer is not straightforward for various reasons.
zh: 而且由于各种原因，答案往往并不直截了当。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe there's confidentiality reasons, maybe there's just somebody is acting on a hunch, but that hunch is informed by years or decades of reps of developing judgment, and they're probably really onto something.
zh: 也许有机密原因，也许只是某人凭直觉行事，但那种直觉是基于数年或数十年的判断力训练 informed by years or decades of reps of developing judgment,而且他们可能真的很有想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not just this kind of arbitrary gut feeling.
zh: 而且这不仅仅是那种武断的直觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: But whatever it is, I really try to get to the bottom of, let me really make sure that I have done my best to understand this person's point of view.
zh: 但不管是什么，我真的试图深入探究，让我真的确保我已经尽力去理解这个人的观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I have some sort of tools for doing that, which I can also talk about.
zh: 我有一些这样做的工具，我也可以谈谈这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if I've done that, and I still disagree, I'm relatively candid about that, but candid in a way where it's still respectful.
zh: 但如果我做了那些，并且我仍然不同意，我会相对坦诚，但要以一种仍然尊重的方式坦诚。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think what you want to avoid is a situation where as a manager you're like, "Ah, I have no control.
zh: 我认为你要避免的是一种作为管理者你会觉得「啊，我无法掌控的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: This sucks.
zh: 这很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: This decision is so stupid, but that's a job, so we have to do it."
zh: 这个决定太愚蠢了，但那就是工作，所以我们不得不做。」

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously that's not going to set your team up for success or make anybody happy about it, but you do hear that, you do see that happening.
zh: 显然，这不会为你的成功奠定基础，也不会让任何人对此感到高兴，但你会听到这种说法，你会看到这种情况发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think what I try to do in those situations is separate out my opinion from it, from the, " Well, what is the insight that makes it make sense to this person" and explain their rationale.
zh: 所以我认为我试图在这些情况下做的是将我的意见从其中分离出来，从「好吧，是什么见解让这对这个人来说讲得通」开始，并解释他们的基本原理。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even if I'm comfortable saying, "I don't necessarily think this isn't how I would do it," or "I don't even really agree with how they're thinking about it, but from their point of view, from their perspective, their professional experience, whatever it is, I could see how this makes sense.
zh: 即使我很舒服地说，「我不一定认为这不是我会这样做的方式」或者「我甚至真的不同意他们思考它的方式，但从他们的角度，从他们的角度来看，他们的职业经验，不管是什么，我能看出这是如何讲得通的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they might be right.
zh: 他们可能是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think they're right, but they might be.
zh: 我不认为他们是对的，但他们可能是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's find out.
zh: 让我们拭目以待。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not going to find out if we are all squabbling about whether this is a good idea the whole time.
zh: 如果我们要一直争论这是否是一个好主意，我们就不会知道结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: The only way we're going to find out is if we give it the best shot that we have and try to do it.
zh: 我们唯一能知道结果的方法就是尽我们最大的努力去尝试并去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we're wrong, that happens sometimes and we try again."
zh: 如果我们错了，这种情况时有发生，然后再试一次。」

speaker: Unknown
en: I like that this comes back to your mental model orientation of, "Here's their mental model, here's what their experience has been like, here's how they see the world, the trends, and then this is why they think the way they think."
zh: 我喜欢这回到你的心智模型导向，「这是他们的心智模型，这是他们的经历，这是他们看待世界、趋势的方式，这就是为什么他们会这样想。」

speaker: Unknown
en: And so instead of encouraging your team or yourself even to be like, "No, no, you're wrong here."
zh: 因此，与其鼓励你的团队甚至你自己说，「不，不，你在这里错了。」

speaker: Unknown
en: It's more, "Okay, here's their data set, let's try this, and this will inform that data set and maybe change their mind."
zh: 不如说是，「好吧，这是他们的数据集，让我们试试这个，这将告知该数据集，并可能改变他们的想法。」

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I think in product, I like to joke, there's no right answers.
zh: 因为我认为在产品中，我喜欢开玩笑，没有正确答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's only wrong answers, and you're just trying to execute well on the least wrong answer that's available to you.
zh: 只有错误答案，你只是试图在你能获得的最小错误答案上很好地执行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think it is the sort of reasonable people can disagree about this stuff at all of this is what I think, and this is how I would approach it.
zh: 所以我认为这是那种理性的人可以对此类事情产生分歧的情况，这就是我的想法，这也是我处理它的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this is what they think and I think this is why they would approach it this way.
zh: 我认为这就是他们的想法，我认为这就是为什么他们会以这种方式处理它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, the only chance we have of succeeding is not being torn apart on that.
zh: 而且，同样，我们唯一成功的机会不是在那上面被撕裂。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so at the end of the day, if it's not a obviously terrible answer, and sometimes even if it isn't obviously terrible answer, you're still more likely to succeed if you just sort of reorient yourself around a world where it's not a terrible answer and then just try to will that into existence.
zh: 所以归根结底，如果它不是一个明显糟糕的答案，有时即使它不是一个明显糟糕的答案，如果你只是重新调整自己围绕一个它不是糟糕答案的世界，你仍然更有可能成功，然后只是试图将其意愿成真。

speaker: Unknown
en: You said that you have some tools to help you understand someone's point of view.
zh: 你说你有一些工具可以帮助你理解某人的观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can't help but ask more about that.
zh: 我忍不住想多问问那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I talk about what I like to call the magic questions, but the thing about magic questions is they're not actually questions, they're statements and they end with, "Do you agree?"
zh: 我谈到我所谓的神奇问题，但关于神奇问题的事情是它们实际上不是问题，它们是陈述句，并以「你同意吗？」结尾

speaker: Unknown
en: Or "Is that right?"
zh: 或者「那是对的吗？」

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I have found this, the most helpful way for kind of trying to understand a person's mental model is to just put facts in front of them and see what they say no to and what they say yes to.
zh: 所以我发现这是试图理解一个人的心智模型的最有帮助的方法，就是把事实摆在它们面前，看看它们对什么说不，对什么说是。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then if you can get them to explain, great.
zh: 然后如果你能让它们解释，那很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if they're good communicators, they often can, but if they're not, you don't have to let that stop you view.
zh: 如果它们是好的沟通者，它们通常可以，但如果它们不是，你不必让那阻止你 view。

zh: 顺便说一句，如果你在波士顿地区，播客世界的各位听众都应该去那里，她很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Shout-out to Emily.
zh: 向 Emily 致敬。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's things like that.
zh: 但就是像这样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just finding these small ways to, because people are already laughing, people are already smiling, we're doing this silly thing, everyone's in a good mood, and I'm like, "Boom, perfect time to give someone a shout-out, and make them feel like a million bucks for doing something, that in many cases, they might think, 'Oh, am I allowed to have this other job outside work?
zh: 这只是找到这些小的方法来，因为人们已经在笑了，人们已经在微笑了，我们在做这件傻事，每个人的心情都很好，我会说，“砰，这是表扬某人的完美时机，让他们因为做某事而感觉好极了，而在很多情况下，他们可能会想，‘噢，我可以在工作之外有这份其他工作吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is this okay?'"
zh: 这行吗？’”

speaker: Unknown
en: And so yeah, you got to proactively build those reward loops.
zh: 所以是的，你必须主动建立那些奖励循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love the reward loop of Emily getting this shout-out right now.
zh: 我喜欢 Emily 现在得到这个表扬的奖励循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is so meta.
zh: 这太元了。

speaker: Hilary Gridley
en: Ultimate reward.
zh: 终极奖励。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have a full class coming up in Boston.
zh: 你在波士顿有一节完整的课要来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there anything else along those lines?
zh: 在这方面还有什么别的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because that was really interesting?
zh: 因为那真的很有趣？

speaker: Unknown
en: And also, people, I know managers already kind of do this, just promoting.
zh: 而且，人们，我知道经理们已经在某种程度上这样做了，只是推广。

speaker: Unknown
en: But so, I think the core lesson here is, focus on things you want to encourage more.
zh: 所以，我认为这里的核心教训是，专注于你想要鼓励更多的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Less so, "Hey, they worked the weekend, they got it done, so awesome.
zh: 而不是，“嘿，他们周末工作，他们完成了，所以太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for doing that."
zh: 谢谢你那样做。”

speaker: Unknown
en: You're saying that's almost an anti-pattern, because you don't necessarily want that as a habit.
zh: 你说这几乎是一个反模式，因为你不一定希望那成为一种习惯。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's more like, shift your reward announcements to things you actually, intentionally want to create, in a new team.
zh: 所以这更像是，将你的奖励公告转移到你实际上、有意想在一个新团队中创造的事情上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, and just be really, really thoughtful about it.
zh: 是的，并且对此要非常、非常用心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, okay.
zh: 是的，好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's come back to the taking care of yourself, because that's something else that came up, almost everyone mentioned this.
zh: 那么让我们回到照顾自己这一点，因为这是另一件被提出的事情，几乎每个人都提到了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're doing a good job with this, of finding time to take care of yourself, and modeling that for other people.
zh: 所以你在做得很好，找到了时间照顾自己，并为其他人树立榜样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Specifically, a lot of people commented on how you create space for creativity.
zh: 具体来说，很多人评论了你如何为创造力创造空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think, to a lot of people, a lot of PMs, especially, is just, "I have no time for anything.
zh: 我认为，对很多人来说，很多产品经理，尤其是，只是，“我没有任何时间做任何事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just have meetings, back to back, all day.
zh: 我只有会议，一天到晚接连不断。

speaker: Unknown
en: I barely have time to go to the bathroom or eat."
zh: 我几乎没有时间去洗手间或吃饭。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm curious to hear just how you do this.
zh: 我很好奇听听你是怎么做到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you create space in your day for creative work, and deep work, and thinking outside of the meeting?
zh: 你如何在一天中为创造性工作、深度工作和会议之外的思考创造空间？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it's funny.
zh: 是的，这很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm glad to hear people think I'm good at this, because I'm terrible at organizing events.
zh: 我很高兴听到人们认为我擅长这个，因为我非常不擅长组织活动。

speaker: Unknown
en: My team's always, "Oh, we should do a fun event."
zh: 我的团队总是说，“噢，我们应该做一个有趣的活动。”

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm like, "Yeah, that's a great idea."
zh: 我会说，“是的，那是个好主意。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I don't organize it.
zh: 然后我就不去组织它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I like to think, I do this in other ways.
zh: 所以我想，我以其他方式来做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I do think one of them is just in modeling, how to carve out space for things, and a couple of things.
zh: 我确实认为其中之一就是通过榜样示范，如何为事情腾出空间，以及几件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's the creativity, which for me is probably more outside of work.
zh: 我认为存在创造力，这对我来说可能更多是在工作之外。

speaker: Unknown
en: For me, it's creativity.
zh: 对我来说，它就是创造力。

speaker: Unknown
en: But again, it's a big part of me as a manager, what I think I can help people with is, back to the point of behavioral activation, understanding what the things are that a person needs to be happy, to be their best self, to be a high functioning person.
zh: 但再说一次，这是我作为管理者很重要的一部分，我认为我能帮助到人的地方是，回到行为激活这一点，理解一个人为了快乐、为了成为最好的自己、为了成为一个高功能的人需要的是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: That depends on their values, it depends on a lot of things about them.
zh: 这取决于他们的价值观，取决于关于他们的很多事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for Emily, it's fitness, it's teaching, it's these things.
zh: 所以对于 Emily 来说，是健身，是教学，是这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: For me, it's having my crafts that I do, my illustration, my writing, my reading, all of these sorts of things.
zh: 对我来说，是拥有我做的那些手艺，我的插画，我的写作，我的阅读，所有这类事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that that's the first step is just, as a leader, understanding what those are for people on your team.
zh: 我认为第一步就是，作为一个领导者，理解团队里的人的那些事是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, as I said, modeling it.
zh: 然后，就像我说的，对此进行示范。

speaker: Unknown
en: I try to always tell people, "Here's how I'm doing these things."
zh: 我试着总是告诉人们，“这就是我做这些事情的方式。”

speaker: Unknown
en: I talk about them, so it's really normalized, because I think a lot of PMs are like, "Oh my gosh, I'm so busy.
zh: 我谈论它们，所以这真的很常态化，因为我认为很多产品经理就像是，“天哪，我太忙了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have no time.
zh: 我没时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm in meetings all day."
zh: 我一天都在开会。”

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's a little bit self-inflicted, I think.
zh: 但这有点自作自受，我认为。

speaker: Unknown
en: At some point, you have to be the one responsible for getting yourself out of the weeds, and it's hard to do, but it is doable.
zh: 在某个时候，你必须成为那个把自己从繁杂琐事中拉出来的人，这很难做到，但是是可行的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think, just showing people that it's possible, showing people that you can do these things.
zh: 所以我认为，只是向人们展示这是可能的，向人们展示你可以做这些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I talk about them, I bring them to lessons.
zh: 我谈论它们，我把它们带到课程里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have a book club that I sometimes require at work, and then I say, "Maybe I don't need to require this anymore," but ways to just make it really visible, make sure people know that I'm doing it, and then ask them about it.
zh: 我有一个我有时在工作中要求的读书俱乐部，然后我会说，“也许我不需要再要求这个了”，但这就是让事情真的可见起来的方式，确保人们知道我在做这件事，然后问问他们关于这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I, in my one on one lens, and I'm checking in with people, I'm asking them, "What do you do for joy?
zh: 如果我在我的一对一视角中，我和 people check in，我问他们，“你为了快乐做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you doing something every single day that's bringing you joy in your life?"
zh: 你是不是每天都在做给你生活带来快乐的事情？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And if they say no, I'm like, "That's a problem.
zh: 如果他们说没有，我就会说，“那是个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are we going to do about that?
zh: 我们要对此做些什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And do you even know what those things are?"
zh: 你甚至知道那些事情是什么吗？”

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I think a lot of people don't, and a lot of people, it's great.
zh: 因为我认为很多人不知道，而且很多人，这很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're like, "Oh, I need to be getting X number of hours of exercise, X hours of sleep.
zh: 他们就像是，“噢，我需要得到 X 数量的锻炼小时数，X 小时的睡眠。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know I need to eat lunch right at 12:00, or else I turn into a pumpkin."
zh: 我知道我需要在正好 12:00 吃午饭，否则我就变成了南瓜。”

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's somebody who knows what all those things are, and you're just there to kind of help them carve out time, that's one thing.
zh: 如果这是一个知道所有那些事情是什么的人，而你只是在那里帮助他们腾出时间，那是一回事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think, and a lot of times, people don't even know.
zh: 但我认为，很多时候，人们甚至不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then you kind of behavioral activation them, where you're like, "All right, well, why don't you try some things, and get back to me, and let me know what seemed to work, what seemed to make a difference?"
zh: 然后你有点像对他们进行行为激活，你会说，“好吧，那你为什么不尝试一些事情，然后回来告诉我，让我知道什么似乎有效，什么似乎产生了影响？”

speaker: Unknown
en: But I do think so much of it is like a permission structure, because people feel the pressure to be like, "Oh, I'm so busy, I'm so busy, I'm in meetings all day.
zh: 但我确实认为其中很大一部分就像是一个许可结构，因为人们感到压力要去表现得像，“噢，我太忙了，我太忙了，我一天都在开会。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can't decline these meetings.
zh: 我不能拒绝这些会议。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can't not do these things."
zh: 我不能不做这些事情。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So in many ways, I think just modeling, it gives them the permission structure to start to take back their life.
zh: 所以在很多方面，我认为只是示范，这给了他们开始夺回他们生活的许可结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: I could see why people love working for you.
zh: 我能明白为什么人们喜欢为你工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Being asked in your one on one, "Have you done anything today that brings you joy?
zh: 在你的一对一中被问到，“你今天做了任何给你带来快乐的事情吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you haven't, that's a problem."
zh: 如果你没有，那就是个问题。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow.
zh: 哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's important.
zh: 这很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's what life's all out.
zh: 这就是生活所关乎的全部。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why are we here, if it's just to toil, and be miserable?
zh: 如果我们只是在这里受苦和悲惨，为什么我们在这里？

speaker: Unknown
en: And also, they will be better people at work, and they'll do better work.
zh: 而且，他们在工作中会是更好的人，他们会做更好的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's, tell me, correct me if I'm wrong, but it feels like that's an element of this.
zh: 我认为这就是，告诉我，如果我错了请纠正我，但这感觉就是这其中的一个要素。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, and it is so funny, because so much of this stuff, it's obvious when you apply it to an athletic context.
zh: 嗯，这太搞笑了，因为这些东西中的很多，当你把它应用到体育竞技环境中时就很明显。

speaker: Unknown
en: And obviously, I talked about the recovery score.
zh: 显然，我谈到了恢复评分。

speaker: Unknown
en: This concept of athletes need to recover is very obvious.
zh: 运动员需要恢复这个概念是非常明显的。

speaker: Unknown
en: No one, I think, would argue with that.
zh: 我认为没有人会反驳那一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're just pushing yourself at 100% of your physical capacity all the time, not only are you going to burn out, but you're literally going to suffer performance decline.
zh: 如果你只是一直以你身体能力的 100% 推挤自己，不仅你会精疲力竭，而且你实际上会遭受表现下降。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in the same way, I think in the athletic world, there's so much more, just acceptance of, I don't even want to say limits, but just like, you have to take the time to do the things you need to be your best.
zh: 同样地，我认为在体育竞技世界里，有更多的，只是接受，我甚至不想说限制，但就像是，你必须花时间做你需要成为最好的自己的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's not just running into the wall all day.
zh: 而那不是整天撞墙。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we forget that at work, but I think the analog is 100% there.
zh: 我认为我们在工作中忘记了这一点，但我觉得类比 100% 存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: I also think about this with, in terms of being able to have creative breakthroughs of any kind, it's just so important to have active rest.
zh: 我也用这一点来思考，在能够拥有任何类型的创造性突破方面，拥有积极休息是如此重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's so important to have heads downtime.
zh: 拥有休息时间真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: This stuff is all very well documented.
zh: 这些东西都有很好的文档记录。

speaker: Unknown
en: We know it all, but we just come up with excuses to not give it to ourselves.
zh: 我们都知道这些，但我们只是找借口不给自己这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's kind of self-sabotage, at a certain point.
zh: 我认为这在某种程度上是自我破坏。

speaker: Unknown
en: I definitely come up with excuses not to do that, and work all the time.
zh: 我肯定会找借口不这么做，并且一直工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I could use this advice myself.
zh: 所以我自己也能用上这个建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's why, here's the thing, here's the thing.
zh: 这就是为什么，重点是，重点是。

speaker: Unknown
en: The Reason I'm so regimented about this is because, if I'm not, I will fall apart.
zh: 我对此如此严格的原因是，如果我不这样，我会崩溃。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's this quote, I can't remember where I saw this, but I love it.
zh: 有这样一句话，我不记得我在哪里看到的，但我很喜欢它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, "I have exercised the demons from my head, but they are outside and they are doing pushups."
zh: 就像是，“我已经把恶魔从我的脑子里赶出去了，但它们在外面，它们正在做俯卧撑。”

speaker: Unknown
en: The threat of the demons coming back is always there.
zh: 恶魔回来的威胁始终存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, I take this stuff really seriously, because I know, if I let myself start to slide into, I'm not doing the things I need to do to take care of myself, I'm going to have a bad time.
zh: 所以，我非常认真地对待这些事情，因为我知道，如果我开始放任自己，不做我需要做的来照顾自己的事情，我会过得很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: The walls are going to start closing in around me.
zh: 墙壁开始向我逼近。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm not shy about that.
zh: 我对此并不害羞。

speaker: Unknown
en: To me, there's no point in torturing myself, and just working so hard, and having no room for joy, and having no room for creativity.
zh: 对我来说，折磨自己，如此努力工作，没有快乐的空间，没有创造力的空间，是没有意义的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even just from a practical standpoint, I'm just not going to succeed.
zh: 即使仅仅从实际角度来看，我也不会成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: This comes back to your point about, I think it was called behavioral activation, doing the thing.
zh: 这回到了你关于的一点，我想这叫做行为激活，做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Instead of waiting for you to feel a certain feeling, do the thing that will make you feel that way.
zh: 而不是等待你去感受某种感觉，去做那件会让你有这种感觉的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: As maybe a final area, but I have a few more questions after this, so maybe not.
zh: 作为可能是最后一个领域，但这之后我还有几个问题，所以也许不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: The final area is AI.
zh: 最后的领域是 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am happy that we waited this long to get deep into AI.
zh: 我很高兴我们等了这么久才深入探讨 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not going to spend a lot of time here.
zh: 我们不会在这里花太多时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: You wrote a whole guest post about this.
zh: 你写了一整篇关于这个的客座文章。

speaker: Unknown
en: You did How I AI to talk through some of this stuff.
zh: 你做了 How I AI 来详细讨论其中的一些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when we were talking earlier, you said that you think people still are completely undervaluing the power AI could have on their ability to learn, and improve themselves.
zh: 但是当我们之前交谈时，你说你认为人们仍然完全低估了 AI 对他们学习和提升自己能力的力量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I know you spent a lot of time on this, with all these GPTs you've built.
zh: 而我知道你在这方面花了很多时间，建立了所有这些 GPT。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just talk about the sense of how much you think people still under-appreciate how much power there is in AI, and helping them become better.
zh: 就谈谈你认为人们仍然在多大程度上低估了 AI 中有多少力量，以及帮助他们变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we are not being nearly creative enough, when it comes to how to think about learning with AI.
zh: 我认为当我们在思考如何用 AI 学习时，我们的创造力远远不够。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think, you hear people worry about entry level jobs, and when you think about an entry level job, it is sort of inefficient by design, because you have taken analyst, sort of a classic entry level role.
zh: 我认为，你听到人们担心入门级工作，当你想到一个入门级工作时，它按照设计是某种低效率的，因为你让分析师，某种经典的入门级角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're doing grunt work, they're doing really tedious work, but they're getting a lot of reps in, because that's exactly how you learn the judgment to do higher level jobs well.
zh: 他们做苦力活，他们做真正繁琐的工作，但他们得到了很多练习，因为这正是你学习如何做好高级工作所需的判断力的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I hear this in creative fields too.
zh: 我在创意领域也听到了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hear this from every, I certainly feel this way.
zh: 我从每个人那里都听到了这一点，我当然也有这种感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: The work that I did in the beginning of my career, it didn't feel like it was all that important, in terms of the impact it was having, but it did feel like it was transformative, in terms of my own judgment and my own taste, and how I think about just making very quick judgment calls.
zh: 我在职业生涯开始时做的工作，就其产生的影响而言，感觉并不那么重要，但就我自己的判断力和我自己的品味，以及我思考如何做出非常快速的判断呼吁而言，感觉它是变革性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, I just wouldn't have been able to do that, if I didn't spend years learning.
zh: 现在，如果我没有花数年时间学习，我就无法做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I used to do social media, the skill of having to condense something that I want to say into 120 characters, or whatever it used to be on old Twitter, 240, I can't remember.
zh: 我过去常做社交媒体，这种技能是将我想说的话压缩成 120 个字符，或者旧 Twitter 上以前的 240 个字符，我不记得了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I forget, actually, isn't that crazy?
zh: 实际上我忘了，那不是很疯狂吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I forget what the original was.
zh: 我忘了原来的数量是多少。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it was 140.
zh: 我想是 140。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, 140 characters, yeah.
zh: 好的，140 个字符，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: 140, I think.

speaker: Unknown
en: It was short.
zh: 它很短。
